public_rationale: A July 22, 2026 report put OpenAI’s projected compute spending through December 2030 at about $750 billion [e1]. OpenAI’s February 27, 2026 disclosure announced a $100 billion expansion of its existing $38 billion AWS agreement over eight years [e2]. Neither item provides a complete, nonduplicated schedule of required payments from August 18, 2026 through February 18, 2030 or December 31, 2030 [e1, e2]. These figures therefore neither establish nor rule out the claimed $800 billion requirement [e1, e2].
limitations: The $750 billion projection comes from a secondary report and does not establish binding payment obligations.
The AWS disclosure does not allocate payments to either claimed window.
The packet lacks complete payment schedules, cancellation terms, capacity conditions and an accounting of overlapping commitments.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI needs at least $800 billion to meet its commitments over the next three and a half years.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI needs at least $800 billion to meet its commitments in the next three-and-a-half years

from_speaker: projected $750 billion in compute spend through 2030
our_interpretation: This is an assertion about commitments already existing when the post was published, rather than a prediction that OpenAI will sign additional commitments.
The target period is the stated payment window: August 18, 2026 through February 18, 2030. The surrounding heading instead names the end of 2030; both readings must be checked.
Needs means gross payments required to satisfy the commitments, before subtracting revenue or existing cash. It does not mean additional fundraising required.
The accounting basis is estimate because the author expressly relies on press reporting and analyst estimates.
criteria.support_condition: Dated contracts, payment schedules, or a sufficiently complete and documented estimate establish at least USD 800 billion of nonduplicated payments required within the stated window under commitments existing at publication.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A sufficiently complete account of those commitments establishes that required payments within the stated window total less than USD 800 billion. A smaller subtotal or spending projection alone does not suffice.

evidence.explanation: This reports projected spending through 2030, not required payments under existing contracts within the claimed window. It neither verifies the additional amount nor establishes an upper bound.

evidence.locator: Section OpenAI to use Trainium compute to power growing Amazon customer demand
evidence.explanation: The primary disclosure confirms a substantial commitment over eight years. Its full value cannot be assigned to the shorter claimed window without a payment schedule.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A complete, documented schedule of commitments existing on August 18, 2026, with required payments through February 18, 2030 and, separately, December 31, 2030. It must distinguish binding obligations from planned spending and remove overlapping amounts.
